about: Working values for a numeric comfort and readability audit. Chosen for mstack as round starting points; NOT copied from any vendor list and NOT read from a primary source. Each one has to be re-sourced from a primary document (the platform's own design guidelines, a published standard or a study) before a fail is treated as final. Taste is not judged here; only geometry.

min_distance_m.unit: metres from the head; nearer UI is hard to focus on
min_distance_m.note: Meta: objects users fixate on for long periods should be rendered at least 0.5 m away; about 1 m is comfortable for menus.

max_distance_m.unit: metres from the head; further UI is hard to read and to point at
max_distance_m.source: mstack working value; re-source from a primary document
max_distance_m.note: working value; no primary source states a maximum. Meta's hands UI page gives roughly 0.8 m to 3 m as the comfortable range for ray-cast UI (https://developers.meta.com/horizon/design/hands-ui-best-practices/).

min_text_angle_deg.unit: degrees of visual angle for the height of a line of text
min_text_angle_deg.source: mstack working value; re-source from a primary document
min_text_angle_deg.note: working value; Meta's display and hands UI design pages give no number for this

max_offset_deg.unit: degrees between the forward direction and an element; further needs a head turn
max_offset_deg.source: mstack working value; re-source from a primary document
max_offset_deg.note: working value; Meta's display and hands UI design pages give no number for this

max_head_locked_offset_deg.unit: degrees off centre for UI that moves with the head
max_head_locked_offset_deg.source: mstack working value; re-source from a primary document
max_head_locked_offset_deg.note: working value; Meta's display and hands UI design pages give no number for this

min_target_angle_deg.unit: degrees of visual angle for the smaller side of something the user points at or touches
min_target_angle_deg.note: Meta gives a minimum angular collider size of roughly 2.5 to 3 degrees (touch and ray); 2.5 is the low end of that range.
